headline: Semi hardware leads all-green into ORCL and ADBE prints; the 9/16 FOMC is a…

sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
## Semiconductor hardware, not rates, carries this tape into next week's software prints
The supported development sits in the chip complex. On the weekly member scan (asOf 2026-09-04) three baskets are green top to bottom: Memory/Storage +7.6% (+7.5% vs SPY, STX/WDC/MU/SNDK), Foundry +5.4% (+5.3% vs SPY, INTC/TSEM/TSM/UMC) and Computer/GPU +3.4% (+3.3% vs SPY, 6 of 6). On the rotation table XLK is the only sector with positive weekly excess (+0.7%). The mechanism this describes is a hardware bid, and the same scan names its limit: Cybersecurity −6.9% (−7.0% vs SPY) and Software/SaaS −4.7% (−4.8% vs SPY) are the two weakest baskets, so the rotation is hardware-over-software rather than a tech-wide bid.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body: The semis-led read holds while credit and vol stay quiet — HY OAS near 2.65, VIXCLS near 14.32 — and while Memory/Storage and Foundry keep their all-green breadth. It breaks if OAS widens past 2.75 for three sessions, if the software drag spreads into hardware on the ORCL/ADBE prints, or if the 9/16 meeting delivers a hike or hawkish hold that reprices the front end. A single ORCL guidance line, given a near-10% implied move, can swing index-weighted software regardless of the chip story.
